text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
LOWELL MASON was born on this day in 1792. He wrote the popular hymn "Nearer My God To Thee".
Australian Postmaster-General FREDERICK DERHAM was born in 1844. He invented the pneumatic tube for sending letters from the Melbourne GPO to the Stock Exchange.
Australian shipping magnate JOHN EDWARD BURKE was born on this day in 1871.
The lovable black Hollywood actress BUTTERFLY McQUEEN was born in 1911. She leapt to prominence in "Gone With The Wind" with her line - "I'se don't know nuthin' bout havin' babies Miss Scarlett!".

ELVIS ARON PRESLEY was born in 1935. Noted for his individual style, influenced by Southern Blues, gospel music, country music and rhythm and blues, he also acted in 33 movies. He died at his Memphis mansion "GRACELAND" in 1977.
Welsh singer SHIRLEY BASSEY, best known for hits such as "Goldfinger" and "Hey Big Spender", was born on this day in 1937.

US guitarist and songwriter with the 'Doors' ROBERT KRIEGER was born in 1946. After the death of JIM MORRISON in 1971 the three remaining group members recorded the LP "New Voices". He then founded the unsuccessful 'Butts Band'.

British rock musician and actor DAVID BOWIE was born in 1947. His real name was DAVID ROBERT HAYWARD-JONES. "Space Oddity" was his first big hit, which was released several times and was successful each time. Further Number one hits included "Fame" (1975), "Ashes To Ashes" (1980), "Let's Dance" (1983), and with MICK JAGGER "Dancing In the Streets" (1985).
** EVENTS **
1800 : The first soup kitchens for the poor were opened
in London.
1889 : New York scientist Dr HERMAN HOLLERITH patented
the first computer.
1915 : Australians were reportedly the greatest letter
writers in the world, sending 500,000 letters and postcards in 1914.
1941 : The founder of the BOY SCOUTS, ROBERT (Stephenson
Smyth) BADEN-POWELL, died on this day. He was born in 1857.
1942 : German troops began retreating from Leningrad,
unable to continue fighting the Russians during the harsh winter.
1948 : Popular Austrian tenor, RICHARD TAUBER, died in
Australia.
1953 : The Australian government signed a ten-year
contract with an American agency for the sale of uranium mined at Rum Jungle.
1963 : Fire damaged seven floors of New York's Empire
State Building.
1973 : Rock idol ELVIS PRESLEY, on his 38th birthday,
sued his wife of six years PRISCILLA for divorce. He recorded a new single called "Separate Ways".
1979 : Vietnamese troops crushed the Khmer Rouge and
occupied Cambodian capital Phnom Penh.
1989 : A Boeing 737 crashed on the M1 motorway in central
England. More than 40 people were killed in the crash after the plane on route to Ireland developed engine trouble.
